title: Model-stitching mismatch triggered hidden fallback paths — postmortem & action items
creator: Asha Menon
description: Summary: On 2025-11-04 we observed a gradual but stealthy quality regression and a correlated cross-region capacity spike that together created a multi-hour degradation for a subset of hosted customers. Root cause analysis shows a model-stitching table inconsistency combined with a non-atomic policy cache refresh path. This allowed a subset of requests to take a previously unseen ‘hidden’ fallback route that doubled requests (duplicate in-flight requests), bypassed rate limits, and triggered cross-region reroutes that amplified load and produced noisy errors for downstream consumers. This ticket collects the incident narrative, root cause, mitigation, and prioritized action items.
timeline:
2025-11-04 08:12 UTC — First alert: elevated 5xx rate from hosted-api in eu-west-1.
2025-11-04 08:20 UTC — Automated routing telemetry shows rising fallback-to-variant-B rates for ModelX-2q for a small customer cohort.
2025-11-04 08:32 UTC — Ops noticed increased outgoing traffic to us-west-2 (cross-region reroutes) and concurrent rise in token usage.
2025-11-04 08:40 UTC — Temporary mitigations applied: increased autoscale headroom in eu-west-1 and rate-limit applied on reroute paths.
2025-11-04 09:05 UTC — Root-cause hypothesis formed: mismatch between model-stitching table and active variant mapping causing policy evaluation to select incompatible fallback edges.
2025-11-04 10:00 UTC — Patch deployed that forced policy cache eviction and enabled atomic policy swap; traffic returned to baseline over next 35 minutes.
2025-11-04 11:00 UTC — Post-incident triage begins.
2025-11-05 — RCA working group formed (runtime, routing, infra, and product).
2025-11-06 — Deep-dive audits of model-stitching updates reveal a race condition in the model onboarding path that can leave transient incompatible "stitches" for up to 45s.
2025-11-10 — Simulated replays confirmed duplicate in-flight request behavior when policy refresh and routing fallback evaluation interleave.
2025-11-12 — This ticket created to capture findings and track action items.
impact: Customer-visible quality regressions (increased wrong-variant fallbacks) for ~12% of requests to ModelX family for affected accounts; capacity spike caused ~2.3x baseline egress to us-west-2 for 40 minutes, increased cost and risk of hitting rate-limits for other tenants. No customer data was exfiltrated. Several high-SLA customers reported elevated error rates; incident severity classified as Sev-2 due to revenue and availability impact.
root_cause_summary: Two concurrent issues combined: (1) a model-stitching onboarding path could write a transient row that maps a model ID to an incompatible variant set (stitch mismatch) for short windows; (2) the routing policy cache refresh was implemented as a non-atomic read-then-swap where in-flight evaluations could observe partially-applied policy state. When the two conditions aligned, fallback evaluation could select a hidden fallback edge that triggered duplicate request paths and cross-region reroutes. This path bypassed the usual per-customer reroute rate limits because the duplicates originated from independent evaluation contexts.
detection: Detected via a spike in per-route fallback rates in the routing dashboards and an anomalous rise in cross-region egress. Instrumentation gaps: we lacked a simple metric for "duplicate-inflight-requests-by-request-id" and the policy-change timeline was not exported to tracing spans, which prolonged diagnosis.
mitigation: Immediate mitigation: forced atomic swap on policy cache and temporarily throttled reroute edges to reduce cross-region amplification. Autoscaling increased to absorb surge. Longer-term hotfix: rolled out a change to make model-stitching updates apply through a staged commit (write-to-temp + atomic-rename) to eliminate transient mismatches.
action_items: RST-1: Implement atomic version tokens for policy updates so evaluations always reference a single consistent policy snapshot — owner: Diego Ramirez — estimate: 3
RST-2: Change model-stitching onboarding to use staged commit (temp write + atomic swap) to prevent transient incompatible mappings — owner: Priya Shah — estimate: 5
RST-3: Add a per-request duplicate-inflight counter and alert when >1 active attempt for same request_id within 5s window — owner: SRE team (lead: Marcus Li) — estimate: 2
RST-4: Add tracing span that records policy snapshot version used for each routing decision — owner: Runtime Observability (lead: Hannah Cole) — estimate: 2

RST-5: Implement circuit-breaker on reroute edges with exponential backoff and per-account egress caps to prevent amplification across regions — owner: Routing team (lead: Diego Ramirez) — estimate: 3
RST-6: Create end-to-end integration tests that replay policy refresh + model-stitching update interleavings to catch races — owner: QA (lead: Naoki Tanaka) — estimate: 3
RST-7: Run a targeted chaos experiment in staging to simulate policy refresh races and cross-region load to validate guardrails before rollout — owner: Reliability Eng (lead: Marcus Li) — estimate: 2
follow_up_tasks: Schedule design review for atomic policy snapshot proposal (link in links) — due 2025-11-18 — owner: Diego Ramirez
Update incident runbook to include explicit steps for throttling reroute edges and checking policy-version consistency — due 2025-11-19 — owner: SRE
Add a throttled synthetic that exercises ModelX fallback paths every 10 minutes to catch silent regressions — due 2025-11-24 — owner: QA
Run cost analysis of the cross-region amplification and propose billing protections for customers affected — due 2025-11-26 — owner: Finance Eng
